topics.topic: Whether and how proxy-only listener reachability must be restricted or verified
questions: What makes an MCP listen address acceptable, and is proxy-only reachability a kernel start-time condition or an unverified host precondition?
What makes or verifies that the configured listener is reachable only by the reverse proxy?
Is proxy-only reachability an unchecked deployment assumption, or must the kernel restrict or verify the configured listener address before starting?

judgement.why: This asks the same proxy-only listener reachability and verification question already decided by P1, with no further relevant text change.

precedent.topic: How reverse-proxy-only listener access must be enforced or verified
quotes: Binding the listener at mcp_listen_address is the last start step and fails the same way, the step named open_entrance, when the address cannot be parsed as a host and port or the socket cannot be bound; a listener lost while serving ends the process with a non-zero exit code, without retry.
precedent.why: State 8 requires a host-and-port listener and restricts startup validation to parsing and binding it, leaving proxy-only exposure as the stated host deployment condition.

topics.topic: Whether the personal-data prohibition includes direct agent-to-service channels
questions: Is the prohibition on an agent receiving personal-data content global, including direct service access, or limited to values returned by the kernel surface?
Does the prohibition on agents receiving personal-data content apply globally, including direct service access, or only to values returned through the kernel surface?
May a service give an agent personal data through the direct channel, or does the owner-only-reader rule prohibit that channel from carrying personal data despite being outside kernel control?

judgement.why: This asks the same question about whether the personal-data rule governs direct agent-to-service access already decided by P2, with no further relevant text change.

precedent.topic: Whether the personal-data prohibition also applies to direct agent access to services
quotes: An agent's own access to a service — as for processing a photo (decision 17) — is granted by that service and the owner outside the kernel; the kernel neither gives nor checks it, and its personal-data promise (K-14) covers what the kernel itself returns.

An agent never receives a `personal_data` value: wherever the surface would return one to an agent, it returns the value's digest and class instead. The owner receives every value. This is one rule of the surface, not a per-agent ceiling and not a redaction inside each operation.
precedent.why: The prohibition is expressly scoped to values returned through the kernel surface and does not govern an agent's independently authorized access to a service.

topics.topic: Manifest facts required to discover the manifest and service repositories
questions: What manifest facts identify the manifest repository and each service repository so that a second agent can discover them from the named sources alone?

topics.topic: What must remain equivalent between rehearsed and production flows across installations
questions: What must be the same between the rehearsed flow on the second installation and the production flow, given that installations have separate records and bindings have randomly minted identities?

topics.topic: Whether agents may directly access outside-sender material still in service intake
questions: May the agent directly read or process outside-sender material while it is still in the service intake, or must a flow operation first take that material from the intake before any direct agent access?

topics.topic: Whether client-to-proxy TLS is a verified requirement or an assumed host property
questions: Is TLS on the client-to-proxy path a required condition that installation or acceptance must verify, or merely an assumed host property?

topics.topic: Whether effectful-flow rehearsal is an enforceable acceptance requirement or recommended practice
questions: Is rehearsal a normative acceptance requirement requiring evidence outside the kernel, or only recommended owner practice with no enforceable or testable obligation?

topics.topic: Whether the security review must cover the direct agent-to-microservice channel
questions: Must the direct agent-to-microservice channel receive an outcome in the State 2 security review, or is A21's completeness claim limited to boundaries controlled by the kernel?
